title: Continuous-batcher slotting and KV eviction strategy for variable-length prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: In production traffic we observe a bimodal distribution of request lengths: short interactive prompts (~32-128 tokens) and long-generation jobs (500-3k tokens). The current continuous-batching scheduler treats all requests similarly which causes KV memory churn and suboptimal slot packing on GPUs, leading to elevated evictions and variability in tail latency.

Objective: Design and validate a scheduler/slotting strategy plus KV eviction policy that improves steady-state throughput and reduces GPU memory fragmentation for mixed-length workloads while keeping P95 latency regressions < 10% for short interactive requests. The implementation must be reversible (feature flag) and include observability and safety fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration gated behind runtime-1.20 feature flag and default-off for Dedicated clusters
>=10% throughput improvement on mixed workload synthetic benchmark with comparable GPU count
KV eviction rate reduced by >=25% on long-tail traffic traces
P50/P95 latency for short requests no worse than baseline +10% and SLO compliance demonstrated in canary
Dashboard with new metrics (eviction_rate, memory_headroom, slot_fill_ratio, tail_preemptions) added to Console
approach: Introduce 'dual-slot' allocator: maintain two slot pools per GPU — small-slot pool for short requests (tight packing) and large-slot pool for long-generation jobs (pre-reserved contiguous KV regions).
Length-estimator at enqueue time: sample first N tokens and use lightweight model/heuristic to classify request into small | medium | long buckets to guide slot assignment.
Soft memory reservation: reserve a small fraction of total GPU KV memory as 'headroom' to reduce fragmentation; headroom can be tuned per-GPU and exposed via config.
KV eviction policy: implement thresholded, model-aware early-eviction for long-run jobs with conservative checkpointing of commonly reused prefixes; prefer evicting lower-reuse KVSlabs first.
Preemption/backpressure: allow preemption of queued long jobs when small-slot pool saturates and short-request latency targets are at risk; return informative throttling errors to clients.
Instrumentation: add token-level KV allocation and deallocation events, per-batch memory delta metrics, and an offline simulator to replay traces and measure fragmentation effects.
decisions: Will prefer a dual-slot allocator rather than fine-grained bucket counts to reduce scheduler complexity and contention.
Length classification runs at enqueue, not at decode loop, to avoid per-token overhead; reclassification only on explicit client signals (e.g., request.max_tokens) or long-running heuristics.
KV eviction will be 'soft first': try warm-prefix checkpointing and slot compaction before hard evictions to avoid quality regressions.
Feature will be rolled out first to a small set of non-production internal tenants and then to canary clusters for Dedicated customers.
open_risks: Classification errors: misclassified long requests placed in small-slot pool may cause eviction storms and latency spikes.
Model quality regressions if KV eviction evicts prefixes that are still semantically important for generation continuity.
GPU fragmentation behavior varies by model and quantization format — heuristics may not generalize across all onboarded models.
Monitoring blind spots: need token-level memory telemetry to diagnose regressions; current agent telemetry is coarse.
tasks: Design doc: draft detailed algorithm and slot metadata layout (Aisha) https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/dual-slot-batcher
Simulator: add trace-replay harness with allocator plugin API for offline tuning (Marco) https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/bench/simulator
Runtime impl: extend scheduler with dual-slot pools + enqueue-time classifier (Eng team) PR# 8342
KV policy: implement early-eviction heuristics and checkpointing hooks (Priya) PR# 8361
Metrics: add eviction_rate, slot_fill_ratio, memory_headroom to Console and runtime traces (Observability)
QA & Perf: run mixed workload sweep, evaluate latency/throughput/eviction trade-offs (SRE/Perf)
test_plan: Synthetic benchmarks: 60/40 short:long traffic mix with multiple models and batch size sweeps
Replay of 7 production traces from last 30 days to measure real-world fragmentation and eviction rates
Canary rollout: 2 Dedicated clusters + hosted internal canary with 1 week stability window
Safety tests: force misclassification scenarios and verify preemption/backpressure correctness
Quality regressions: run eval prompt suite and measure generation divergence metrics after early-evictions
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated in runtime-1.20; default-off for customer clusters
Internal canary (non-prod) for 48 hours with automated rollback on P95 breaches >10%
Dedicated canaries: two low-traffic tenants for 1 week
Gradual ramp to 25% of traffic with close SRE monitoring; automated kill-switch if eviction_rate > baseline * 1.5
Full enablement after 4-week observation and postmortem of any incidents
